name: Excess-Solution (Wet) Impregnation - Metal on Oxide Support
description: The support is slurried in an excess volume of precursor solution and equilibrated, then separated by filtration/decantation before drying and activation.

step_quantities.note: Support slurried in excess precursor solution
Solid-liquid separation. Sub with plate and frame at small scale
Calcination. Sub with batch kiln at small scale

route_note: Costs more than incipient wetness for the same loading: it needs downstream solid-liquid separation, carries a larger solvent inventory, and loses precursor with the mother liquor. Precursor loss is a raw-material effect the step model does not yet price - only the extra equipment time is captured here.
source: Jimenez et al., Industrial Catalyst Impregnation: Modern Equipment, Techniques, and Scaling Challenges, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 65, 12447 (2026)
